column1: What does a sparse autoencoder do?
column2: Re-expresses each activation as a combination of a few of many learned features: f = ReLU((h − b)W + c), rebuilt as fW' + b, with an L1 penalty on f.

column1: What did the SAE change here?
column2: Single-mindedness rose from 51% for raw neurons to 82% for features, explaining 83% of neuron activity.
A bigger L1 penalty gives fewer active features (easier to read) but rebuilds the neurons less well, and leaves some features dead.
A feature firing on many different words of one kind, e.g. city names before a full stop, or digits, or sky words.
